2611.32710.title: Red-Teaming a Sovereign LLM, Its Reasoning and Its Training Stages
2611.32710.paper_summary: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for applications with sensitive information. We investigate whether confidentiality instructions in system prompt can protect such information. We red-team Apertus v1.5, an open sovereign LLM, and five other model families across six languages and reasoning modes. We use synthetic personal records to evaluate direct disclosure, correction baits, yes/no verification, derived-value queries, reasoning leakage and authorisation checks. We also explore copyright attribution, historical misrepresentation and stereotyping. Despite confidentiality instructions, Apertus 8B and 70B leak information in 96% and 95% of requests, respectively, in correction-bait attacks. Verification and derived-value queries also expose protected information without necessarily revealing identifiers. Moreover, reasoning traces can leak confidential records even when final answers withhold them. Our experiments also show that post-training does not consistently improve safety. Our findings demonstrate that system prompts alone cannot ensure confidentiality and highlight the need for multilingual reasoning-aware safety evaluations.
2611.32710.author: Hatef Otroshi Shahreza et.al.
